title: Cellular Respiration
standard_text: Aerobic respiration: glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain; the role of mitochondria and ATP; anaerobic respiration in plants and animals (alcoholic and lactic acid fermentation); uses of anaerobic respiration in industry. (summary of the senior secondary Biology curriculum, SSS 2; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 Biology worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): respiration, aTP and comparing the processes, glycolysis and the Krebs cycle, electron transport and fermentation and anaerobic respiration. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Anaerobic respiration releases much less energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Respiration releases energy from glucose, which is stored in ATP. Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm and splits glucose into pyruvate; in aerobic respiration the pyruvate enters the mitochondria, where the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain produce most of the ATP, carbon dioxide and water.

Without oxygen, cells respire anaerobically. In muscles, pyruvate becomes lactic acid, causing fatigue. In yeast, it becomes ethanol and carbon dioxide (alcoholic fermentation), which is used to make bread and beer.

Example

Where does the Krebs cycle happen?

The powerhouse of the cell

Answer: in the mitochondria

Example

What does yeast make in anaerobic respiration?

Fermentation

Answer: ethanol and carbon dioxide

Common mistakes

  • Thinking respiration is the same as breathing.
  • Thinking plants do not respire.
  • Thinking anaerobic respiration makes more energy.

faq.a: Yeast respires and releases carbon dioxide, which forms bubbles in the dough.

faq.q: Why do you breathe hard after a race?
faq.a: To supply oxygen to break down the lactic acid (the oxygen debt).

items.q: What is made in anaerobic respiration in human muscle?
items.e: Yeast makes ethanol and CO₂ instead.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 4 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 4 = 8.

items.q: Which molecule can be respired if glucose runs out?
items.e: Fatty acids enter as acetyl CoA.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 2 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 4 ATP.

items.q: What is the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration?
items.e: Oxygen combines with electrons and protons to form water.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 7 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 7 = 14.

items.q: Why is potassium hydroxide used in a respirometer?
c: it absorbs the carbon dioxide produced
items.e: So the change in volume is oxygen taken in.

items.q: An organism takes in 45 cm³ of oxygen and gives out 31 cm³ of carbon dioxide. Calculate the respiratory quotient.
items.e: RQ = CO₂ given out ÷ O₂ taken in = 0.689 (1.0 for carbohydrate, about 0.7 for lipid, about 0.9 for protein).

items.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in mammals?
items.e: Pyruvate is reduced, regenerating NAD.

items.q: What is a limiting factor?
c: the factor that is in shortest supply and so controls the rate
the factor that is present in excess
the temperature at which an enzyme denatures
a factor that stops a reaction for ever
items.e: Light, CO₂ and temperature limit photosynthesis.

items.q: An organism takes in 40 cm³ of oxygen and gives out 32 cm³ of carbon dioxide. Calculate the respiratory quotient.
items.e: RQ = CO₂ given out ÷ O₂ taken in = 0.800 (1.0 for carbohydrate, about 0.7 for lipid, about 0.9 for protein).

items.q: What happens in the link reaction?
c: pyruvate is oxidised to acetyl CoA, releasing CO₂ and reducing NAD
items.e: It takes place in the matrix.

items.q: Why does anaerobic respiration make much less ATP?
c: only glycolysis produces ATP; the Krebs cycle and electron transfer chain stop
items.e: Only 2 ATP per glucose.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 6 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 6 = 12.

items.q: Why is a respirometer kept at constant temperature?
c: temperature changes gas volume and enzyme activity
items.e: Use a water bath and a control tube.

items.q: Which is used in respiration if carbohydrates run out?
items.e: Fats enter as acetyl CoA, proteins as amino acids.

items.q: What is the first product of the Krebs cycle?
items.e: Acetyl CoA + oxaloacetic acid → citric acid.

items.q: Which enzyme makes ATP in the inner mitochondrial membrane?
items.e: Protons flow through it.

items.q: Where do the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place?
c: on the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast
items.e: Chlorophyll is in the thylakoids.

items.q: What is the word equation for aerobic respiration?
c: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (+ ATP)
items.e: It releases energy as ATP.

items.q: What is the name for the enzyme that fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells of C₄ plants?
items.e: PEP carboxylase: the enzyme that fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells of C₄ plants.

items.q: A competitive inhibitor slows an enzyme. How does it work?
c: it has a similar shape to the substrate and blocks the active site
items.e: Adding more substrate reduces its effect.

items.q: Where does the Calvin cycle take place?
c: in the stroma of the chloroplast
items.e: It uses ATP and NADPH.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 1 molecule of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 2 ATP.

items.q: What is the first stable product of the Calvin (C₃) cycle?
items.e: It has three carbons.

items.q: Which wavelengths of light are absorbed most by chlorophyll a?
items.e: Green is reflected.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 6 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 12 ATP.

items.q: What do the light-dependent reactions supply to the Calvin cycle?
items.e: Water is split and oxygen is released.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 5 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 10 ATP.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 8 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 8 = 16.

items.q: What is the first stable product in C₄ plants?
items.e: It has four carbons.

items.q: Why do C₄ plants show almost no photorespiration?
c: CO₂ is concentrated around RuBisCO in the bundle sheath
items.e: So RuBisCO works as a carboxylase.

items.q: What is the word equation for photosynthesis?
c: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (in light, with chlorophyll)
items.e: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

items.q: Where does the electron transport chain of aerobic respiration take place?
c: on the inner membrane (cristae) of the mitochondrion
items.e: Most ATP is made here.

items.q: About how many ATP are made from one glucose in aerobic respiration?
items.e: Anaerobic respiration gives only 2.

items.q: Where does glycolysis take place?
items.e: Glucose is split into two pyruvate.

items.q: Why is anaerobic respiration much less efficient than aerobic respiration?
c: it makes no ATP at all
glucose is only partly broken down, so much less ATP is made
items.e: Energy is left in lactate or ethanol.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 7 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 14 ATP.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 10 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 10 = 20.

items.q: What is PS II?
c: the enzyme that fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells of C₄ plants
the cycle in the stroma that fixes CO₂ into sugar
a reaction centre chlorophyll an absorbing best at 680 nm (P680)
RuBisCO binding O₂ instead of CO₂, wasting energy
items.e: PS II: a reaction centre chlorophyll an absorbing best at 680 nm (P680).

items.q: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in the complete aerobic respiration of 6 molecules of glucose?
items.e: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O: 36.

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidise 3 molecules of glucose completely?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 acetyl CoA, so 2 turns: 6.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP from glycolysis of one glucose?
items.e: 4 are made but 2 are used.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 3 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q: Where in the cell does fermentation take place?
items.e: Fermentation: the cytoplasm, without oxygen.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 5 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in the complete aerobic respiration of 3 molecules of glucose?
items.e: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O: 18.

items.q: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in the complete aerobic respiration of 10 molecules of glucose?
items.e: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O: 60.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 2 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 2 = 4.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 1 molecule of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidise 6 molecules of glucose completely?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 acetyl CoA, so 2 turns: 12.

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidise 9 molecules of glucose completely?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 acetyl CoA, so 2 turns: 18.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 9 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 9 = 18.

items.q: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in the complete aerobic respiration of 1 molecule of glucose?
items.e: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O: 6.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 9 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 18 ATP.

items.q: Where in the cell does glycolysis take place?
items.e: Glycolysis: the cytoplasm.

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidise 4 molecules of glucose completely?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 acetyl CoA, so 2 turns: 8.

items.q: Where in the cell does the electron transport chain take place?
items.e: The electron transport chain: the inner mitochondrial membrane.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 3 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 6 ATP.
